timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Welcome to the wonderful world of chemistry.
Today with the help of chemistry of materials set from male chemistry,
you will produce a liquid which solidifies when pouring it from one cup to another.
Perform this experiment on a plastic tray to contain any possible spills.
Don't forget to put on protective gloves and goggles before doing the experiment.
To open a bottle containing a region, push the cap down and turn it.
Pierce the bottle nozzle with an unbent paper clip.
For the silicate plastic experiment, you will need two disposable cups,
calcium hydroxide, liquid glass solution, a plastic syringe and some water.
Pour the entire bottle of calcium hydroxide into the first plastic cup.
Using the syringe, add 15 milliliters of water to the cup and mix the contents with a swirling motion.
Pour the solution of liquid glass into the second cup.
Now pour the liquid back and forth from one cup to the other until the mixture solidifies.
Calcium hydroxide reacts with sodium silicate, the main component of the liquid glass.
As a result of this reaction, water insoluble calcium silicate forms and the mixture solidifies.
Learn more about this experiment on our male chemistry website.

youtube_description:
Perform this amazing experiment at home with MEL Science: https://melscience.com/en/experiments/inorganic-plastic/

Safety
* Put on protective gloves and eyewear.
* Conduct the experiment on the plastic tray.

Disposal
Dispose of solid waste together with household garbage.

Step-by-step instructions
1. Take a disposable cup and pour in calcium hydroxide Ca(OH)₂ from the bottle (3 g). Add 15 mL of water.
2. Thoroughly mix the contents in the cup.
3. Take another cup and pour in 50% liquid glass solution from the bottle (10 mL).
4. Now, pour the liquid from the one cup into the other and back.
5. The liquid has solidified! Keeping your protective gloves on, touch the obtained mass.
